Mid-moment: Su Wan's silhouette stands at the far end of a dimly lit midnight police corridor, back to camera, nearly motionless in waiting. Her frame is small at distance, reduced by perspective depth, dark outline against the amber emergency lamp glowing at the corridor end. One foot shifted slightly forward, weight patient but tense. The fluorescent overhead lights flicker intermittently, casting unstable shadows across her silhouette. The burgundy accent of her toenail polish catches the amber emergency light from distance—the only warm color point in her dark form, glowing like a signal in the darkness. She is watching for Lin Ze or awaiting his decision, her stillness reading as coiled rather than relaxed. Captured as if shot by Wong Kar-wai for through_gap composition—the distance and obstruction (wall frame edge left foreground) making her both present and psychologically unreachable. The corridor stretches behind her toward the lamp. Her silhouette reads as patient predator in stillness, or lonely figure in institutional void—the ambiguity is the point. The flickering fluorescent creates temporal hesitation; the fixed amber lamp creates singular endpoint focus. Her burgundy accent echoes act1_start_02 but at distance becomes abstracted—same motif, new emotional register: from intimate Hitchcock close-up to distant Wong Kar-wai tableau. She does not move. She waits.

The phone vibrates mid-frame as an incoming call displays on screen—the caller ID "陈局" (Commissioner Chen) appears in amber-tinted text. The hand is in mid-decision posture: fingers not yet moving to answer or reject, knuckles showing pressure pallor from grip intensity. The phone screen gloss reflects the corridor floor geometry as an abstracted line of shadow and light at frame bottom. Fluorescent light from above washes the back of his hand, creating cool bluish tone contrast against the warmer skin of palm. The hand's weight presses downward as if the phone itself has become heavier with the decision it represents. The vibration is continuous, implying the phone has been ringing for a moment already—the hand is already committed to holding the call, just not yet to answering it. No tongue, no mouth visible. Only hand as decision instrument. Captured as if shot by Wong Kar-wai for the temporal hesitation before choice—the frame freezes the kinetic moment between stimulus and response. The phone vibration is audible in the tactile tension of his grip. The corridor institutional line reflected in screen glass becomes metaphor: even this small device carries the entire institutional pressure system. This is Mamet constraint: the phone IS the entire scene.
